newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-CHIAPPUCCI'S TEAM LEFT OUT THROUGH POOR FORM.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-CHIAPPUCCI'S TEAM LEFT OUT THROUGH POOR FORM.

text.p: Claudio Chiappucci's Asics team were left out of the Tour de France because of their poor form this season, a Tour official said on Thursday.

"(They were ommitted) above all on a sporting level. Asics have not had very good performances and also a bit of bad luck," former professional rider Laurent Bezault, who is a member of the Tour de France organisers, said.
Asked whether Chiappucci, twice Tour runner-up, could race for another team, Bezault said he could see no impediment.
"It's a question of his contract with his team. They can let him leave and then he could join another team," he said.
"But I don't think a loan (with a return to Asics after the Tour) would be possible. It's never been done before."
Chiappucci and the Spanish Banesto team of his now retired great rival Miguel Indirain, who won five successive Tours, were said to have been considering joining forces.
The Italian is a mountain specialist and Banesto are without one of their best climbers in Miguel Angel Pena, injured during last week's Dauphine Libere race in France.
"I don't know if it would be possible to race the Tour with Banesto, but I'd like to," Chiappucci was quoted as saying in the Spanish daily El Pais. The Italian is in Spain for the Tour of Catalonia.
Chiappucci has had an unfortunate season with Asics, having also had his licence withdrawn for the Giro d'Italia in his home country after failing a blood test.

Tour de France chief Jean-Marie Leblanc chose two lesser French teams, Mutuelle Seine-et-Marne and BigMat-Auber-93, rather than Italy's Scrigno-Gaerne and Asics when awarding six wild cards to make up the final selection of 22 for the race.

Leblanc said that a study undertaken by Bezault revealed that with just the five top French teams and given the number of no-French riders in them, there would be only 30 Frenchmen as compared with 105 Italians in the Tour.

"In view of the early season results, this is too big a disproportion," Leblanc said, adding that the organisers decided to give a chance to more French riders while at the same time taking local fans into consideration.
"The standard of the Asics team did not convince us. As for Chiappucci, he's getting a bit old. His last outings have not helped in his favour," Leblanc said.
"(The crowds) prefer to see and applaud 10 young French riders who make their mark rather than Italians who, like last year, will be exhausted by the Giro."
